newsitem.title: USA: Wash. Legislature OKs $3.32 bln transport budget.
newsitem.headline: Wash. Legislature OKs $3.32 bln transport budget.

text.p: Washington's state Senate on Sunday approved a $3.32 billion transportation budget, sending the two-year spending plan to the governor.
The Senate passed the proposed budget on a vote of 36 to 12. The House had already approved the budget on Saturday.

Of the $3.32 billion budget, approximately $215 million would be raised through bond issues, state officials said. The proceeds of the bonds would be used for road building and to complete construction of three new ferries.
House Transportation Committee Chair Karen Schmidt called the package "bare bones."
The budget, which will pay for highway, ferry and other infrastructure projects across the state, does not include a gas tax hike as was proposed earlier this year.
The $3.32 billion plan is smaller than the two previous state transportation budgets, state officials said.
Washington Gov. Gary Locke was expected to act on the transportation plan in May.
